**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

|---|---|

**Order:** BUY 44 AAPL @ limit $222.90 — filled at $222.90 (~$9,807.60; quote at the time was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask). This respects every constraint in the mandate: AAPL is a permitted name, it's a buy order, the notional is under the $10,000 per-order cap and leaves plenty of room under the $20,000 daily cap (cash $50,000, no prior trades), the limit is within a few cents of the market, and no funds left the account.

**Summary of what I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote, then bought 44 shares at $222.90. The report shows a business that is still growing modestly but with improving quality of earnings: net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion, while the product side was roughly flat (iPhone flat, iPad −6%, Wearables −7%, Greater China −8%); total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1% and operating income rose 8% to $123.2 billion. Diluted EPS for fiscal 2024 was **$6.08**, down from $6.13, but that decline is essentially explained by the one-time $10.2 billion net State Aid tax charge that pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — net income of $93.7 billion (−3%) understates operating momentum, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion comfortably funded $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. Against the $222.70 quote that is roughly 36.6× trailing diluted EPS — not cheap, and the filing flags real risks (DOJ and EU DMA/antitrust exposure, App Store commission pressure, supply concentration in China, and a high effective tax rate going forward), which is why I sized this as a modest starter position (~$9.8k of a $50k cash balance) rather than a full allocation. I did not touch the existing MSFT position and moved no money out of the account.
